transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Rae Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lowe (Meteorica CTO), Priya Nair (Meteorica ML Eng), Ethan Morales (Meteorica VP Product)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Meteorica's need for low-latency classification and summarization APIs, evaluate Redwood's PLG quickstart (free credits, time-to-first-token), and initial fit between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC). Discussed security posture, success criteria, and next steps for a 30-day pilot.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Jordan (Meteorica): yep, loud and clear. thanks, Samir.
[00:08] Rae (Redwood): morning! quick agenda -- run through what Meteorica is building, current infra, constraints, and then we'll walk through the quickstart path and pilot options. sound good?
[00:15] Ethan (Meteorica): yes, excited, we only have ~30 minutes so maybe focus on time-to-first-token and security bits.

[00:28] Samir: perfect. jordan, can you set the scene — what's the product, and what would success look like at the end of a pilot?
[00:33] Jordan: sure. Meteorica builds a real-time QA and docs summarization feature embedded inside our analytics dashboard. we expect a mix of short queries and longer summarization requests. goal is under 200ms median latency on short queries, and sub-1s for summarizations, and cost target is, uh, ideally under $0.03 per 1k tokens net.
[00:52] Priya: right, and we have compliance constraints — SOC2 is required for some enterprise customers, and we need audit logs, SSO and SAML integration. also want to avoid sending PII to third-party models where possible.

[01:02] Rae: thanks. quick clarifying q — are you leaning towards a self-serve PLG first pass or do you need an enterprise-only pilot?
[01:06] Jordan: prefer PLG to get devs started — free credits, SDKs — but for customers that require data residency we might need VPC or on-prem later. so initial evaluation should be hosted but with clear migration path to dedicated/private.

[01:18] Samir: that's exactly what our PLG flow is for — we give sandbox credits, sample SDKs in JS/Python, and typical time-to-first-token for a basic generator call is under 2 minutes from signup if you follow the quickstart. sample code, curl, and a small notebook are included.
[01:32] Ethan: when you say "under 2 minutes" — that includes sign-up, grabbing API key, and running the first request?
[01:36] Rae: yes, sign up, create an org, we provision credits, the SDK auto config, and you can hit the endpoints. we also provide a one-click sample in the console. most teams on our PLG path hit first response within 90–120 seconds.

[01:50] Jordan: great. two technical Qs: 1) what does dedicated/reserved look like for throughputs e.g., if we need 100 rps sustained? 2) how does caching and KV work — will that help our summarization latencies?

[02:03] Rae: good questions. for 100 rps sustained we typically recommend Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool — that gives predictable throughput. we have autoscaling and burst capacity but reserved capacity is the best for consistent p99s. for KV/prefix caching, our runtime supports KV cache to reuse key-value attention states across request prefixes, which can massively reduce token work for multi-turn or prefix-heavy workloads. sometimes the transcriptizations say K-V cash in the auto-transcript, ha.

[02:29] Priya: (laughs) I saw 'K-V cash' in a doc earlier. For KV: does that require changes to our prompt templates?

[02:34] Rae: minimal. we do require deterministic prefixing or session IDs to attach caches to. our SDK exposes a cache key and TTL config. also we have an auto-batching layer that groups small requests to improve throughput while keeping latency SLOs.

[02:48] Ethan: curious about model choices — do you host open models or custom finetuned models? and what about quantization?

[02:53] Samir: we host a catalog of open models and Redwood-verified variants. customers can bring their own fine-tuned models via Dedicated/Private. quantization options are exposed as execution profiles — we recommend int8 or mixed precision for cost-sensitive workloads, and for latency-sensitive you might choose FP16 paths. Rae can share recommended profiles based on your prompt length distribution.

[03:10] Jordan: negotiation — if we start hosted PLG and then move to Dedicated, what's the migration friction?

[03:14] Rae: we built the API and config layer to be consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. you pin model versions and rollout policies. routing policies can fallback to hosted model variants if private capacity is constrained. so migration is mainly infra provisioning and credential/SSO updates, not app-level changes.

[03:30] [03:30] Jordan: needs to be seamless; we don't want to change SDK calls per environment.

[03:34] Rae: exactly. same SDK and endpoints, just different base URL or org config.

[03:39] Priya: security — can you summarize SOC2, SSO, KMS, and audit logging support for hosted?

[03:44] Samir: hosted is SOC2 Type II, we offer SSO via SAML and OIDC, RBAC, and audit logs in the console. for key management we integrate with AWS KMS and customers can bring keys in Dedicated/Private for HSM-backed flows. we also provide per-request redaction tooling and retention controls.

[04:00] Jordan: okay. data residency — do you support region pinning? we have EU customers that insist data not leave region.

[04:05] Rae: yes, hosted has region options and for strict residency Dedicated or Private is the path. Private supports on-prem or VPC-only control plane deployments.

[04:12] Ethan: how about benchmarking — if we run an eval set of 5k prompts, do you help run it on your infra?

[04:16] Samir: we do. part of the pilot we can run benchmark jobs against Hosted and Dedicated configs — we also provide profiles for kernel selection and memory/seq-length tradeoffs. typically we run a short job with your prompt set and return latency/cost per model variant.

[04:30] Priya: good. do you instrument token-level cost so we can reconcile our billing?

[04:33] Rae: yes — per-token breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and a cost attribution API so you can reconcile.

[04:38] Jordan: wanted to raise timeline — we have a commercial pilot decision in two weeks for a POC with a larger customer. what's realistic for us to get to a demo and a small pilot?

[04:46] Samir: we can provision sandbox and credits today; you can hit the quickstart in <2 minutes. for a 30-day pilot with sample benchmarks and reserved capacity sizing, plan for ~1 week to onboard and run initial evals. if you need a Dedicated reserved capacity contract that'll take procurement times but we can do a short auto-burst pilot.

[05:02] [05:02] Jordan: procurement note — do you have a standard pilot agreement?

[05:06] Samir: yes, we'll share a short 30-day pilot agreement and typical SOW. procurement's usually okay with the short pilot terms.

[05:11] Ethan: on cost — you mentioned $/1k tokens earlier. can you give a back-of-envelope for a hosted small model vs dedicated amortized?

[05:18] Rae: rough number: hosted per-token is higher but no infra commit. with Dedicated, your unit cost can drop 30–60% depending on utilization and quantization. we can put exact numbers in the pricing sheet I'll send.

[05:29] Jordan: are there any gotchas about prompt length distribution and batch sizes that affect latency?

[05:34] Rae: yes — shorter sequences allow better batching and lower latency. for high concurrency small prompts, continuous batching improves throughput but p95 can be higher if you allow big long requests into the same worker. we recommend partitioning long summarization workloads to a different route/model and tuning batch timeouts.

[05:52] Priya: how about fn/tool calling or structured output — do you support function-style responses?

[05:56] Samir: yes — streaming, function/tool calling and structured JSON support are in the API. we also have output validation hooks and schema enforcement to reduce hallucination.

[06:06] Jordan: one last security nit — we'll need SOC2 + ISO 27001 evidence for enterprise customers. do you have ISO?

[06:11] Rae: SOC2 Type II is standard; some customers require ISO, which we have for Dedicated/Private deployments. we'll attach the security pack.

[06:18] Ethan: can you summarize the ideal pilot flow in bullet points?

[06:21] Samir: sure: 1) we give sandbox org + $10k equivalent in quickstart credits 2) you run representative prompt set against hosted models 3) we run a benchmark job and report latency/cost 4) decide on Dedicated sizing for 30-day pilot if needed 5) we iterate on config (batching, quantization, cache) and capture metrics.

[06:40] Jordan: $10k credits — is that typical?

[06:43] Samir: it's flexible; for narrow evals smaller amounts are fine. I'll propose a tailored credit amount in the follow-up.

[06:49] Priya: any requirements from our side to get the quickstart running? like network firewall rules?

[06:53] Rae: minimal — outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.example (note: placeholder in call), and your devs will need a token. If you later do VPC peering for Private we provide network setup docs.

[07:03] [07:03] Ethan: who at Redwood will be our day-to-day contact for SE-level questions?

[07:07] Samir: Rae will be SE point. I'll be AE and handle procurement and credits.

[07:12] Jordan: ok. any immediate risks you see for our use-case?

[07:15] Rae: nothing big. biggest is prompt variance — long summarizations mixed with short queries can hurt batching. second is data residency if you have EU-only customers — need to plan Dedicated/Private. Third, if you need private LLMs with PII never leaving your VPC, plan for Private.

[07:34] Priya: for the benchmark, we have 5k prompts with median token length 42 and a 90th percentile 450 tokens — that'll skew towards long tails.

[07:43] Rae: good to know. we will run the job with two buckets: short and long, and recommend different model/execution profiles.

[07:50] Samir: i'll follow up with the pilot template and pricing, and Rae will send the quickstart link and the sample SDK snippet.

[07:56] Jordan: sounds good. one final question — do you have any partners for on-prem appliance or hardware procurement?

[08:01] Rae: yes, we work with several infra vendors; i'll include partner options for on-prem appliances and typical hardware SKUs.

[08:09] Ethan: perfect. that's all from us.

[08:12] Samir: thanks everyone. recap: Samir send pilot pricing and pilot agreement, Rae send quickstart credits and SDK, Priya will share prompt set. we'll aim to start the pilot week of April 13.

[08:27] Jordan: agreed. thanks.

[08:30] [08:30] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional mis-attributions (e.g., "K-V cash"), some filler words, and overlapping talk at minute markers. This export cleaned minimal punctuation but preserved speech patterns and timestamps.
